# v0.30.0 — storing each message once across retries, replays and restarts

This release works toward “nothing lost”: storing each message once across retries, replays and restarts. Each batch of incoming messages commits or rolls back as a unit. The release also preserves more changed history and marks repeated stored copies. Known loss and duplicate-storage limits remain below.

New recall presentation options, entity memory and pre-compaction extraction stay off by default. The next-stage message classifier is planned for v0.30.x. No answer-quality gain is claimed for this release. v0.30.0 is the code of its sixth and final release candidate, v0.30.0-rc6, with these notes added, and its qualification on that candidate is reported under **Qualification**. The release gate passed. Some rows are not green, each by a disclosed decision: D5 and the reference-agent window, D2, D3, D1 with local embeddings, two test-kit rows and the D6 rows other than its `OFF` recall row (all not run; D1 and the full D4 and D8 rows run after the release), the Phase B probe matrix and host-suite comparison, two bars each of Phase C and D5-B, D7's facts-kept bar (recorded, not judged), three crash and fault cells that keep raw FAILs as known issues and three that are unsupported, and the busy-session check, which failed ([#2293](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2293)).

## On by default in this release

- **Atomic ingest with a shadow ledger.** Ingest is the step that stores incoming host messages. Each batch records message bindings, observed timestamps and the conversation view in its own transaction. The shadow ledger records evidence alongside the current message classifier; `LCM_INGEST_LEDGER=off` disables those records; a cold start then no longer skips rows the ledger proves stored (see **Identity-anchor switch** under **Upgrade**) ([#2055](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2055)).

Compaction summarises older context. The fixes under **Changes since v0.29.1** apply without a new setting unless they describe an optional tool or feature. Replay links mark stored copies; a link does not remove either copy.

## Upgrade

- **Host and Python.** Hermes 0.21.3 or newer is required, with 0.21.5 or newer recommended. Python 3.11 or newer is required. Advisory checks against upstream Hermes do not make it a supported host.
- **Store schema.** The schema version stays 5, with no new columns in `messages`. The shadow ledger adds `ledger_meta`, `occurrence_bindings`, `ledger_emissions`, `stamp_observations`, `ingest_views` and `lineage_marks`; recording delegated-child ancestry also adds `session_lineage`. These are additive tables in the existing store ([#2055](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2055)).
- **New settings.** `LCM_INGEST_LEDGER` defaults to `shadow`. The new recall options default to `false` for `recall_adjacent_reply` and `recall_summary_event_time`, `score` for `recall_delivery_order`, and `0` for `recall_snippet_window_hits` and `recall_extra_entries`; their environment variables and effects are under **Optional features**. Upgrading from v0.29.1 also brings v0.29.2's `LCM_SHUTDOWN_COMPACTION_WAIT_S` (default 10 s).
- **Removed condensation and transcript cleanup.** Cache-friendly follow-on condensation and transcript garbage collection are removed. `LCM_CACHE_FRIENDLY_CONDENSATION_ENABLED` and `LCM_LARGE_OUTPUT_TRANSCRIPT_GC_ENABLED` remain parsed but are ignored, with one warning per process when enabled. Existing garbage-collection placeholders remain readable ([#1246](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1246)).
- **Deferred maintenance is deprecated.** `LCM_DEFERRED_MAINTENANCE_ENABLED` still works and defaults to off, but enabling it adds a warning in `/lcm status`, `lcm_status` and the `lcm_doctor` configuration check. Removal is planned for v0.31.0. `LCM_DEFERRED_MAINTENANCE_MAX_PASSES` applies only while it is enabled ([#1246](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1246)).
- **Host message identifiers stay in shadow.** `LCM_HOST_MESSAGE_UID` defaults to `shadow`. The next-stage classifier and its identifier-based decisions remain planned for v0.30.x.
- **Identity-anchor switch.** New in v0.30.0: with the ingest ledger at its default (`LCM_INGEST_LEDGER=shadow`), a cold start no longer stores again the rows it can prove it already holds, also when `LCM_IDENTITY_ANCHOR=0`. An operator who used the anchor switch to make LCM-X store every incoming row again now also sets `LCM_INGEST_LEDGER=off` ([#2055](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2055)).
- **Rollback.** Take a SQLite-safe backup before upgrading. The rollback target is v0.29.2. Rolling back loses no rows. One case stores a copy: a tool result that Hermes saved to a file, which v0.30.0 stores in full, is stored once more with its tool call the first time v0.29.2 replays that history; see **Known issues** ([#2552](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2552)).
- **If you ran a v0.30.0 release candidate.** v0.30.0 is the code of rc6 and does not rewrite rows that a candidate stored:
  - **rc1 to rc5:** a row that a candidate stored while its payload file could not be written, or with redaction on (see **Changes since v0.29.1**), keeps the form that candidate gave it. A session that holds such a row can still lose its last rows when it ends while another session is active, and a delegated child can still store that row again. Two more effects apply to a row stored with redaction on: when the same tool call is handed to LCM-X again, its result is stored once more, once; and from then on that session’s older turns are no longer summarized, because compaction cannot match the two forms. No row is lost, the session’s rows stay stored and searchable, and a new session is not affected; the fix is planned for v0.30.1 ([#2604](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2604)). A store written only by v0.29.2 on a supported Hermes holds no such row.
  - **rc1 to rc4:** a delegated child’s session can hold extra copies of a tool result that Hermes had saved to a file. Later candidates and v0.30.0 leave those rows in place and add no new ones. The two duplicates listed under **Known issues** can still add a copy ([#2558](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2558), [#2559](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2559)). A session that ended while another was active, after a saved tool result, can be missing its last rows; no release can bring those back, because Hermes does not send an ended session again.
  - **rc1, rc2 or rc3 on a store that v0.29.2 had written:** a conversation replayed under those candidates can hold one extra tool call and result for each saved-output marker. Later candidates and v0.30.0 leave those rows in place. A fresh upgrade from v0.29.2 to v0.30.0 does not create them, except in the two cases of the upgrade duplicate listed under **Known issues** ([#2558](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2558)).

## Changes since v0.29.1

This release also contains every v0.29.2 fix, including the new `LCM_SHUTDOWN_COMPACTION_WAIT_S` setting (default 10 s). They are described in the v0.29.2 notes and not repeated here.

### Restarts, retries and replay links

- **Compaction snapshots survive carry updates.** Maintaining carried message ranges keeps the record of message occurrences tied to its compaction proof. After a restart, an equal-content retry with a changed timestamp or message ID is still stored ([#1451](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1451)); the rest of #1451 stays open for v0.30.x, see **Known issues**.
- **Recovered user turns have visible replay copies.** After a restart, possible replay copies of a recovered user turn are marked. New requests with the same text remain stored ([#1523](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1523)).
- **Failed identity reads retry classification.** If an identity-anchor read or timestamp backfill fails after the host changed messages before the resume point, ingest rolls back and classifies once more. A persistent fault keeps the previous fallback, and a busy retry remains available; no row is lost ([#1815](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1815)).
- **A replayed tool result is stored once.** After a restart, a resume point between a stored call and its result no longer causes the result to be stored twice. The skip requires an identical, directly following stored result, matching timestamps and an unused earlier occurrence; results without that evidence are stored ([#2163](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2163)).
- **Ambiguous restart copies are marked.** When a restart re-sends an already stored batch from the start, each repeated row gets a `possible_replay_of` link to the oldest unused matching row in the same session. Matching tries exact content before content with reasoning blocks removed, and refuses different known timestamps. Exact copies made only of reasoning blocks are linked too ([#2305](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2305), [#588](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/588)).
- **Rotation replay links cross the recorded chain.** After a fit-only session rotation that has no child commit proof, a cold resend still stores earlier sessions’ rows again, but now links each copy to its earlier row, except the re-emitted summary marker, which has no saved original. Linking checks the current session first and stays within the conversation’s recorded ancestors. For a 32-hop chain and 2,000-row resend, the write-lock hold rose from 183 ms to 272 ms at the 90th percentile; median ingest time was 1.58 times `v0.29.2-rc1` in that benchmark ([#2029](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2029)).
- **Changed timestamps keep their provenance.** Re-stamped carried turns link to their earlier occurrences after compaction and rotation, including originals in a predecessor session and first copies stored by a rotation child. Prompts that inherited a carried timestamp, or were later stored at their own timestamp, also get links. Rows with the same replay identity but different content link to their own originals ([#2378](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2378), [#2390](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2390)).
- **Borrowed timestamps get a replay link.** When the host shows the next user prompt with the timestamp of the prompt in flight during compaction, the later stored copy gets one `possible_replay_of` link. The earlier copy remains available for other replay links; neither row is skipped or changed.
- **Each copy gets one replay link.** The cursor-zero replay scan and session ancestry adoption no longer add a second replay link to a row already linked by an earlier step ([#2305](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2305)).
- **An interrupted helper agent keeps its rows.** A delegated child that is interrupted before it finishes now keeps its rows up to its last completed save, which runs before each of its model calls. This covers every helper agent that runs its own LCM-X engine, as helper agents do on the supported Hermes versions, while that engine still serves the profile the helper agent started with; otherwise its rows are saved only when it finishes, as before, and one WARNING says so. Before this release, an interrupted child kept none of its rows ([#2482](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2482)).
- **A saved tool result is stored in full and recognised when Hermes sends its marker again.** Hermes saves a too-large tool result to a file and leaves a short marker; v0.30.0 stores the file’s content in a payload file of its own. Two markers are the same row only when their text is identical; a marker is the same row as a stored full result when the file path and character count recorded at ingest agree with the marker’s, and the marker’s preview is exactly the start of the stored content ([#2539](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2539), [#2546](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2546)). If that payload file cannot be written (a full disk, or a payload folder that cannot be written to), LCM-X stores the marker exactly as the host sent it, which is what v0.29.2 stores for a file under Hermes’s home; the row stays a marker after the fault clears ([#2599](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2599), [#2602](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2602), picked onto the release branch in [#2613](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2613)). With sensitive-pattern redaction on (off by default, `LCM_SENSITIVE_PATTERNS_ENABLED`), a result saved under Hermes’s home whose preview holds text that redaction rewrites is stored as its marker, redacted, as v0.29.2 does ([#2603](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2603), [#2606](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2606), picked onto the release branch in [#2616](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2616)). The limits of this matching, its costs and what a replay can still store again are under **Known issues** ([#2544](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2544), [#2604](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2604), [#2605](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2605)).

### Compaction and changed history

- **Delegated children no longer lose a new row when the compression boundary is missing.** After a failed pre-compaction store, a failed boundary record or a concurrent store, a later row that repeats the last stored row no longer causes a new row to be lost. A child resumes at its last stored row only when all preceding rows are stored in its ancestry or are outputs of its last compaction. It stores other preceding rows along with the later rows and warns with their count. The compaction-output record is kept only in memory, so after a restart the child's compacted head is stored one extra time (a duplicate; nothing is lost). A new row with the same content and role as an older stored row still cannot be told apart from it; other limits are under **Known issues** ([#2071](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2071)).
- **Busy pre-compaction writes skip the pass.** If a delegated child cannot store its input because the database is locked or busy, compaction returns `noop` with `compaction skipped: input not stored`. The next pass stores the full view first. Other write failures still lose rows removed by compaction, as disclosed under **Known issues** ([#2306](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2306), [#2440](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2440)).
- **Moved tool rows are stored within a bounded history.** When the host changes messages before the resume point and the audit also finds a missing row there, LCM-X stores moved tool calls and their results. This applies to standard tool-call records across the session and its verified or recorded predecessors, within 10,000 stored rows, 15 million stored-text bytes and 10,000 tool-call entries. All three bounds must hold; the remaining shapes are listed under **Known issues** ([#2455](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2455), [#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467)).
- **Host folds and task-list snapshots replay safely.** Assistant folds anchored to stored parts and unstamped task-list snapshots already held in the session are recognised as replays, including batches replayed from the start. Original bytes and timestamped user snapshots stay stored; ambiguous or over-budget shapes remain new. Treating an unstamped task-list block as generated host text requires timestamped-prompt evidence, and later edits and proven rewinds survive optional-read failures.
- **Task-list provenance survives session end.** Exact task-list snapshot replays after session-end flushes get links without suppressing new snapshots. Stored host task-list composites record ordered `composite_of` provenance when their whole-row decomposition is unique, without changing ingest or replay decisions. After a conversation ends and resumes, a to-do list merged with your next message is not linked yet; see Known issues ([#2488](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2488)).
- **Ignored-message placeholders stay out of stored history.** A compaction pass clears its message-to-store-ID map when it finishes. A later ingest can no longer mistake a reused memory address for that old mapping and store a carried ignored-message placeholder as a real row ([#2344](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2344)).
- **Merged human text stays visible.** On hosts without a model-only display key, LCM-X clears a stale `model_only` marker from generated rows in a mixed user group. The merged human text stays visible ([#1436](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1436)).

### Recall and tools

- **Memory names have a length limit.** `lcm_memory` now rejects a `name` or `aliases` entry longer than 256 characters, and its schema states the limit ([#1944](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1944)).
- **Read-only store access over MCP.** `scripts/lcm_x_mcp.py` (the `lcm-x mcp` reader) serves `lcm_recall`, `lcm_grep`, `lcm_expand`, `lcm_load_session` and `lcm_describe` to Claude Code through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) over standard input and output. It needs a source checkout of this repository, because a catalog install does not include `scripts/`. Register it with `claude mcp add` and the Hermes venv Python (3.10 or newer); see the operator guide. It opens one Hermes store read-only per call, uses production schemas and outputs, and returns `store_uuid` plus degraded-mode flags. Unless a writer stamped an ID, it derives one from file identity and reports `store_uuid_source: derived`; it does not alter Hermes stores ([#1192](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1192)).
- **Full-text search is retried once when it timed out and nothing else was found.** When full-text search runs out of its share of the time budget and the semantic searches return nothing, `lcm_recall` now runs full-text search once more inside the request’s deadline instead of returning no evidence. Such a response carries `provenance.fts_rerun` ([#265](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/265); test `tests/test_issue_265_recall_fts_rerun.py`).
- **Search and recall include the current session’s delegated children.** `lcm_grep` with its default scope also searches the current session’s delegated child sessions, recall treats those children as part of the current session when it ranks, and a hit from a child carries `parent_session_id` and `lineage` ([#1931](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1931); tests `tests/test_issue_1931_delegate_children.py`, `tests/test_subagent_lineage.py`).
- **Summary rows are read by column name.** On a store whose summary table has an older column order, summary timestamps and expand hints are now read correctly, which can change the order of summary hits ([#635](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/635); test `tests/test_issue_635_dag_decode_by_name.py`).

### Operator tools and diagnostics

- **Doctor and backup respect ingest transactions.** `/lcm doctor clean apply`, `/lcm doctor repair apply`, backup flushes and doctor full-text-search integrity checks take the store write lock. They wait for a multi-row ingest to commit instead of rolling back or partly committing its rows ([#2345](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2345)).
- **Pending raw-flush counts are explicit.** The session-end warning reports `unflushed=unknown` while the ingest cursor awaits reconciliation. The count is described as a cursor-based estimate, rather than a durability count ([#1364](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1364)).
- **Session decisions and storing routes are logged.** Per-engine INFO logs identify binding and bypass rules and the first store or skip, without message or pattern text. Every ingest that stores rows also emits a content-free `LCM ingest route:` line, at INFO for the `cold`, `session_end`, `persisted_batch`, `warm_tail` and `S3` routes and at DEBUG otherwise ([#2042](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2042), [#2305](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2305)).
- **Successful child resumes stop reporting false fallbacks.** Successful delegated-child resumes and store-only turns log at DEBUG. They no longer add false fallback counts or skipped-ingest warnings; storage is unchanged ([#2074](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2074)).

### Integration documentation

- **Companion hook timing is scoped to its evidence.** The separate Claude Code integration’s 0.1.0 notes distinguish drain time, pointer-file stalls and hooks stopped by the host. They scope measured figures to the recorded runs and point to the release’s own result card. They also clarify search modes, configuration-dependent paths, local cleanup audit fields and temporary-file handling ([#2350](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2350)).

## Optional features

- **Adjacent replies in recall.** `recall_adjacent_reply` / `LCM_RECALL_ADJACENT_REPLY` defaults to `false`. Enabling it places next-turn replies after the best raw recall hit and the top three question hits, within existing hit and size caps. It is read-only and deadline-bounded; internal recall and session delivery keep their behaviour.
- **Summary event-time ranges.** `recall_summary_event_time` / `LCM_RECALL_SUMMARY_EVENT_TIME` defaults to `false`. `lcm.recall_summary_event_time: true` in `config.yaml` also enables it, with the environment taking precedence. Model-called `lcm_recall` summary hits and session-delivery summary leads get `event_time_start` and `event_time_end` from source messages’ earliest and latest host `observed_at`, including condensed sources. It never uses write times. The fields are absent when no source has a host time. A carried timestamp adds `time_uncertain: "carried"`. A non-strict `answer_ready` summary then stops taking a message’s `event_time`. Failed or late reads set `provenance.summary_event_time_unavailable`. Internal recall and benchmark output keep their behaviour.
- **Recall hits in time order.** `recall_delivery_order` / `LCM_RECALL_DELIVERY_ORDER` defaults to `score`. Set it to `time` to deliver the same selected `lcm_recall` hits from oldest to newest by host observation time, with untimed hits and summaries last. Session delivery and internal recall keep their existing order.
- **Wider recall snippets.** `recall_snippet_window_hits` / `LCM_RECALL_SNIPPET_WINDOW_HITS` defaults to `0`. The first N message-excerpt hits get windows of up to 2,400 characters, centred on the matched chunk, keyword match or query match. Shorter messages return whole. Ranking, selection, proactive recall, `detail="answer_ready"` and `delivery_unit="session"` keep their behaviour. Larger windows can fit fewer hits under `response_char_cap`, reported as `response_cap_truncated`. Failed or late window reads retain the original snippet and set `snippet_window_skipped` to `read_error` or `deadline`.
- **Compact extra recall entries.** `recall_extra_entries` / `LCM_RECALL_EXTRA_ENTRIES` defaults to `0` and is capped at 25. Snippet-hit delivery appends at most the smaller of that cap and half the delivered limit, rounded down, as 300-character extras from later ranks. It skips duplicates without refill. The candidate pool, rerank window and `total_results` keep their existing sizes. Extras carry only `kind`, `store_id`, `session_id`, `event_time`, `window` and `extra=true`. Late or failed reads set `extra_entries_skipped` to `deadline` or `read_error`. Internal recall, answer-ready and session delivery ignore the setting.
- **Extraction stops at its deadline.** Pre-compaction extraction, `LCM_EXTRACTION_ENABLED` / `extraction_enabled`, still defaults to `false`. Its absolute deadline now also bounds the host stream, so a slowly streaming extraction stops at that deadline ([#1149](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1149)).
- **Event recorder.** `LCM_RECORDER_ENABLED` defaults to `false`. Enabling it writes what the host asks of LCM-X to local files under `LCM_RECORDER_DIR` (default `$HERMES_HOME/lcm-recorder/`), so a run can be replayed offline against another build. All recorder writes are capped by `LCM_RECORDER_MAX_BYTES` (default 20 GiB). Restart the host to change these settings. The recorder needs Python 3.12 or newer; on Python 3.11 the flag logs one warning and installs nothing ([#2243](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2243)). A checkpoint that comes due once the exit drain has begun is skipped, counted as `recorder.checkpoint_skipped` and warned, so the recorder does not hang the exit ([#2512](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2512), [#2511](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2511)); the recorder guide says which Hermes exits run Python’s exit handlers.

## Known issues

Loss limits come first. Fixes are planned for v0.30.x unless a different release is named. “Resume point” means the position through which LCM-X believes it has already examined the host’s messages.

- **An interrupted helper agent can lose the rows after its last save.** A helper agent's rows are saved before each of its model calls; the hook waits at most 2 seconds for the save, which then finishes in the background. A save that cannot finish (a database that stays busy, an error) leaves its rows to the helper agent's next save or its end. If the process ends before a save has stored them, the rows since the last stored save are not saved. This happens while its tools run: that round's tool call and finished results stay only in the host's database. It also happens while a save waits more than 5 seconds on a busy database at shutdown, and then one WARNING gives the number of rows not yet saved. Every earlier row is saved for a helper agent that runs its own LCM-X engine, while that engine still serves the profile the helper agent started with. Otherwise, and for a helper agent without its own engine, the rows not yet saved are saved only when the helper agent finishes, so an interruption loses them, as before this release. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2482](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2482), [#2483](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2483)).
- **New messages after a host-shortened history are lost.** If the host shortens the conversation on its own, such as an undo followed by a compression request that compacts nothing, later new messages are treated as already stored and are not saved. Which hosts produce this shape is not established. A second known route is Hermes's message-sequence repair, which runs only when message alternation is broken and rewrites the list in place: if LCM-X ingests the repaired, shorter list before the next new message, that next user message is not stored. No run has shown this route yet. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1525](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1525)).
- **Repeated text is under-stored on partial-history hosts.** After a restart and compaction, a host that sends only new messages loses occurrences of text repeated within the session. The reference agent sends full history. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2124](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2124)).
- **Repeated compacted-out tool pairs are lost.** On hosts that reuse tool-call IDs, a new call and result identical to a pair compacted out of view are treated as a replay after a cold restart and are not stored. The already-shipped fix for a pair still in view does not cover this shape. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)).
- **Busy session end with undo and resend leaves a message unstored.** With ignore patterns configured, a busy session end followed by undo, resend and an ingest that changes nothing leaves the earlier occurrence pending and counted at exit, but not stored ([#2247](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2247)). Separately, without ignore patterns, any busy session end followed by an undo and resend also keeps the earlier occurrence pending, counted and reported at exit rather than stored. Only a host resume of that session recovers it; `/new` does not. ([#1838](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1838), [#2206](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2206)). Planned fix: v0.30.x.
- **An ignored-message placeholder makes a later loss silent.** If ignore patterns are or were configured and the session-end view contains an LCM-X ignored-message placeholder, a busy session end followed by undo and resend loses the earlier occurrence. Session end logs a pending retry, but the later drop is neither counted nor reported. v0.29.x lost the same message on this trigger but warned at session end that final messages might be missing; this release no longer gives that warning. No ignore patterns are set by default. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2474](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2474)).
- **Untimestamped replacements before the resume point are lost.** A host merge or replacement before the resume point drops an unstamped new row; if an entirely unstamped view replaces all rows at the same length, none of the new rows is stored. On Hermes this follows undoing every turn or retrying a one-turn session when no host database exists or its transcript write failed; timestamped rows are stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#7](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/7)).
- **Some moved tool rows are still skipped.** A moved tool call or result before the resume point is not rescued when the audit finds no missing row there. The audit never examines tool rows on its own: a tool call and result replaced before the resume point are lost, and a pair inserted there stores its result without its call ([#2452](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2452)). Tool groups that cross the resume point while their unstamped results were already stored also retain the old skip behaviour. Affected new rows are not stored; planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467); fixed in this release on turns where the audit also misses a row inside the presence window, [#2455](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2455)).
- **Large or non-standard tool histories keep the old loss behaviour.** The moved-tool check does not run beyond 10,000 stored rows, 15 million bytes of stored text or 10,000 tool-call entries across the session and its ancestry. It also falls back for the whole scope if any stored tool-call format is non-standard: call entries must be objects with text IDs and text arguments. New moved rows left classified as positional replays are not stored, and one INFO line reports the limit; planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467); fixed in this release on turns where the audit also misses a row inside the presence window, [#2455](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2455)).
- **Externalized arguments and reused IDs bypass the moved-tool fix.** A call whose arguments are externalized at ingest reads as a reused ID, including an inline data URI with at least 256 base64 characters, a run of at least 4,096 base64-alphabet characters, or line-wrapped base64. Reused IDs, repeated call or result IDs in the view, and argument comparisons beyond the 256,000-byte parsing budget retain the old replay decision, leaving affected new call or result rows unstored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172), [#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467)).
- **Replaced unstamped replies and scaffold-looking replies are lost.** If a reply reaches LCM-X without its host timestamp and the host replaces it before the resume point (an edit-and-resend in a long session), the replacement is not stored while the session runs. A restart stores it, together with copies of the session's other unstamped replies ([#2479](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2479)). Replies that carry their host timestamp, as Hermes sends them unless a session has no host database or a transcript write failed, are stored. Planned fix for this part: v0.30.x ([#2116](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2116)). A reply carrying `CONTEXT SUMMARY` markers is still treated as LCM-X scaffold while the engine is running, and lossy-redacted rows still count as replays. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467)).
- **Unreadable ancestry limits moved-row recovery.** If presence reads fail, ancestry cannot be verified with `state.db` present, or a rotation-predecessor write failed in the current process, only rows found by the existing audit are stored. Other rows before the resume point remain classified as replays and affected new rows are not stored; a warning reports the fallback. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467)).
- **Identifier-only replacements behind a merged summary are lost.** When the host changes only a message’s unique ID behind an unchanged merged scaffold, the cached prefix consumes the proof and the replacement is not stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1428](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1428)).
- **A new occurrence at an alternate timestamp is lost.** Once the original host view is gone, a new event with identical content at a previously recorded alternate timestamp is not stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1519](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1519)).
- **Earlier edits inside a shortened view are lost.** If a host shortens its view and edits an earlier row in place, LCM-X does not store that edit. This also occurs in v0.27.0. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1563](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1563)).
- **A retried result with only a new ID is lost.** After a cold restart, a retried tool result whose only change is its unique message ID is dropped. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1837](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1837)).
- **Identical new tool pairs after restart are lost.** A new call and result identical to an earlier stored pair are treated as a replay after restart and are not stored. If the restart follows a stored rewrite of the earlier result, the old call is also stored again beside that rewritten result without a replay link. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2377](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2377), [#2414](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2414)).
- **Pasted scaffold-shaped user turns are lost.** A user turn that starts with the preserved-objective prefix or quotes a whole summary part is skipped when there is no current version-4 compaction proof, including before any compaction, under older proofs or after a cold rebind retires a stale proof. A task-list-prefix turn is affected in every proof state; before any compaction, such turns are skipped after restart even at the tail, or while running when before a stored row. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2110](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2110), [#2418](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2418)).
- **Equal user identities hide a new occurrence.** In a delegated helper agent's session with many equal user messages, after a restart, a failed compaction step or a host head rewrite, a recorded boundary that becomes ambiguous on the next view lets an older copy count against a new one. One occurrence is not stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2422](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2422)).
- **A warm view that starts with a tool call can store nothing.** When a warm ingest gets a view that starts with a tool call and does not extend the previous view, none of its rows is stored. No host path is known to produce this view. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2419](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2419)).
- **Non-busy pre-compaction write failures lose child rows.** When a delegated child’s input write fails for a reason other than a locked or busy database, such as a disk or I/O error, compaction still removes rows from its view and those raw rows are lost. Their stored summary is the only trace, and `compression boundary not recorded: input not stored` warns about the failure. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2440](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2440)).
- **Multiple timestamp conflicts after busy session end lose messages.** After a busy session end with no later ingest, two or more messages whose host timestamps conflict with saved copies can be lost. If a later ingest brings the same messages unchanged, they are kept and counted instead. v0.29.2 has the same limit. Planned fix: v0.30.x.
- **A same-second resend under a new platform ID is lost.** After a cold restart, a new turn with the same text in the same second as an earlier one, under a new platform ID, is taken as the earlier turn and is not stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1037](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1037)).
- **A repeated tool step after a rewind can be missed, with an identical message after it.** After a restart, if a conversation was rewound and the agent repeats exactly the same tool call with the same result, followed by a message identical to an earlier saved one, all three are taken as a replay and are not saved, even when the host's timestamps show they are new. We know of no way to trigger this from Hermes today. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2259](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2259)).
- **One half of a re-dated tool pair can be saved without the other.** After a restart in a conversation that LCM-X has compacted, if the host re-dates only one half of a saved tool call and its result as new, that half is saved and its partner is not. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2191](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2191)).
- **Messages pending at a busy session end are missing after a gateway stop until you resume.** If a session end found the database busy and the gateway stops before a retry succeeds, the messages still pending are missing from the store until you resume that conversation. After /new they are not recovered. The only sign is the warning logged when the session ended. The fix needs a change in Hermes ([#2253](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2253)).
- **Under heavy two-writer contention, a session end finds the database busy more often than on v0.29.2.** Our busy-session check with a second writer failed: 19 of 20 session ends were busy against 13 of 20 on v0.29.2 (the limit is 18), and 18 of 20 against 12 of 20 (limit 16) with a partial fix that ships later. On a 2,000-row batch the write lock is held about 2.3 times as long (2.29 against a 2.25 tripwire, also a FAIL; 1.8 times on a first batch), and the second writer’s ingest waits about 1.4 times as long at p95 on that bench. A busy session end keeps its last messages in memory and stores them at the next session start or end, at shutdown or at a normal exit. They are lost if the process is killed or crashes first, or if the database stays busy through the exit retry (the gateway-stop case is [#2253](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2253)), and v0.30.0 opens that window more often than v0.29.2. The fix is planned for v0.30.1 ([#2293](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2293)).
- **Messages can be missing if the database stays busy from a session end until the process ends.** If the database is busy when a session ends, stays busy at every later retry (the next session start or end, a related session's start, and the 5-second shutdown drain), and the process then dies or exits while it is still busy, the session's last messages are not saved. They are saved only if you resume that conversation; /new does not recover them. Every busy session end and every failed retry is logged and counted. This is an accepted limit; fixing it needs a journal outside the database.
- **A few restart cases keep messages pending instead of saving them.** After a busy session end, LCM-X keeps a conversation's newest messages pending, rather than risk saving them in the wrong place, in three more cases: a single message that the host re-dates newer than its saved copy; a view rewritten after later messages were saved; and, when the session's binding is ignored or stateless, a message with a different known timestamp. Pending messages are counted and reported at engine shutdown or a normal exit (not after a gateway stop; see [#2253](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2253)), but they are saved only if you resume that conversation. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1838](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1838)).
- **An identical message re-sent in place is taken as a replay.** On hosts that send no message IDs or timestamps, a message re-sent with exactly the same text in the same place, so the conversation does not get longer, cannot be told apart from a replay, and it is not saved again. The same holds when a shortened conversation grows back with identical messages, and for identical overlapping messages in a migration or a full-history replay. This is a design limit: telling them apart needs message IDs or timestamps from the host.
- **Some Desktop sessions can end with nothing saved.** Some sessions started from the Desktop app can end with no messages saved. The cause is not known yet; this release logs each session's storing decision to help find it. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2042](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2042)).
- **The last rows of a session can be lost when its end is not written at once.** When a session ends while another session is the active one, or while the store is busy, LCM-X stores its last rows only if the rows it already holds match what the host sends. They do not match if the host changed an earlier message of that session. An earlier row that holds an inline encoded block (line-wrapped base64, or a data URI, inside a tool call's arguments or inside list-form content) can also fail that comparison, even when the host re-sends it unchanged, because LCM-X moved the block out at ingest. The rows after that point, usually the final reply, are then not stored. When another session was the active one, no warning is logged; at most an INFO line says the session was skipped. When the store was busy, LCM-X warns that the end is queued for a retry, warns once more when the retry finds the mismatch, keeps the rows pending, and counts and reports them as not stored at a normal exit. This also occurs in v0.29.2, which in addition can lose the final reply when the store is busy at a session's end, even without such a block. Planned fix: v0.30.1 ([#2543](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2543)).
- **A saved tool result replaced in place keeps its first content.** If a host replaced a large tool result in place, under the same call ID and with the same size and opening text, LCM-X keeps the content it stored first and does not store the new content. For a session that ended while another was active this is the same as v0.29.2. It also applies to the rows of a delegated helper agent, which v0.30.0 stores for the first time. No supported Hermes path is known to replace a result this way, from a reading of Hermes's tool-result storage code ([#2544](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2544)).
- **A turn with a tool call nested about 2,000 levels deep is not stored.** If a tool call's arguments are JSON nested about twice Python's recursion limit deep (2,000 levels with the default limit of 1,000), LCM-X fails while reading them. No row of that turn is stored, and no later turn is stored while that call stays in the history the host sends. For a delegated helper agent no row of that handover is stored, and none of any later handover that still holds the call; rows from earlier handovers stay stored. The host sees no error; the only trace is a warning in the log. No real tool call is known to nest this deep, but nothing prevents one. This needs Python 3.12 or later; on Python 3.11 the arguments stay unparsed text and the turn is stored. The main-session case also occurs in v0.29.2. Planned fix: v0.30.1 ([#2583](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2583)).
- **When a host replaces an unanswered tool call under the same call ID, a new call that differs only in how a number is written is taken as the stored call.** LCM-X can store a tool call at the start of a turn, before its result exists. If the host then sends that turn again with a call under the same ID whose arguments differ from the stored ones only in the spelling of a number, and both spellings read as the same 64-bit float, LCM-X keeps the stored call, does not store the new call's row, and stores its result. That is intended for one number written two ways (1.0 and 1.00). It also happens for two different numbers that read as one float: 0.1 and 0.10000000000000001, or 1e400 and 2e400. v0.29.2 stores neither the new call nor its result in this case. No supported Hermes version is known to replace a call under the same ID. Planned fix: v0.30.1 ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)).
- **With payload externalization turned off, a saved tool result is not recognised as the stored row.** This needs a non-default setting (`LCM_LARGE_OUTPUT_EXTERNALIZATION_ENABLED=false`). LCM-X then stores the marker of a saved tool result with lines of its own added, and that row never matches the marker the host sends again, so the saved-result matching of this release does not apply. When such a session ends while another session is the active one, or while the store is busy, the rows after that result, usually the final reply, are not stored. v0.29.2 loses the same rows with this setting. In a delegated helper agent's session the result is also still stored again on each model call, with nothing marking the copies. Keep payload externalization on, as it is by default. Planned fix: v0.30.1 ([#2547](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2547)).
- **With redaction on, a result saved in the system temp folder can cost a session its last rows.** Sensitive-pattern redaction is off by default. With it on, when the preview of a tool result that Hermes saved in the system temp folder holds text that redaction rewrites, LCM-X cannot pair the stored row with the marker Hermes sends again. If that session ends while another session is the active one, the rows that arrive with its end, usually the final reply, are not stored. v0.29.2 does the same. Hermes saved results there only up to 0.20.4, and LCM-X supports Hermes 0.21.3 and later, so no supported setup is affected; a result saved under Hermes's home is not affected ([#2604](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2604)).
- **A hard kill in the middle of a turn can leave that turn's rows only in the host's database.** Only in a conversation that has a compaction child: one compacted by Hermes's legacy rotating compaction (`compression.in_place: false`; the default is in-place compaction), now or earlier. Over the ACP transport, on Hermes v0.21.6 to v0.23.1 (run on the released builds v0.21.7 and v0.22.2 and on two pinned upstream builds, under a deterministic fault; the other releases in the range by our reading of the source): if the host process is killed hard in the middle of a turn, the restarted host resumes the conversation as it was before its first compaction and never hands that turn's rows to LCM-X. At risk are the rows of the turn in flight that the host has saved and LCM-X has not yet stored. LCM-X stores a turn's rows at the end of the turn, so that is the user's message, any tool calls and results saved so far, and, for a few milliseconds, the final reply. Those rows stay in the host's database, are absent from LCM-X's store, and are not recovered automatically in v0.30.0. Rows of completed turns are not affected. A conversation that was never rotated is not affected: in the default in-place mode LCM-X stores the interrupted turn at the next load. v0.29.2 loses the same rows: under a deterministic fault the same rows were absent on both versions in all 36 runs (18 pairs). In our scripted probe the gap between the host's save of a reply and LCM-X's was about 4 to 13 ms at the median (tails up to about 100 ms) and about 1 to 2 ms longer at the median on v0.30.0. With a kill aimed at that gap, v0.30.0 lost the reply in 19 of 72 runs and v0.29.2 in 12 of 72 (14 against 4 on one build, 5 against 8 on the other). Hermes 0.21.5 and earlier are not affected. After a hard kill, if a conversation is never loaded again, the rows of its interrupted turn that were not yet stored can stay only in the host's database, on any host and in any mode. The fix, which reads the stranded rows back from the host's database at the next start of that conversation, is scheduled for v0.30.1 ([#2624](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2624)).
- **A rare message loss after two compactions in a row is under investigation** ([#2330](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2330)): in one run of the reliability test matrix, two messages that arrived right after a compaction rotated the session were never stored, because a second compaction ran in the new session before the turn ended. It has not been reproduced: the failing cell was repeated 8 times on the same host with full logging, and all 8 passed. v0.29.2's notes list the same lead. If it recurs, that run's stores and logs are kept for the fix, which ships in a later release.
- **A hook-only delegated child can rebind its parent's engine.** This is traced in the source only: it has never been observed, and no test covers it yet. Planned fix: v0.30.1 ([#2066](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2066)).
- **A store that a v0.30.0 release candidate wrote can still lose a session's last rows.** A row that a candidate stored while its payload file could not be written, or with redaction on, keeps that form, and a session that holds it can lose its last rows when it ends while another session is active; an early candidate's session can be missing its last rows for good. See **Upgrade**. Planned fix: v0.30.1 ([#2604](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2604)).

These loss shapes are also tracked, each in its own issue, which sets its fix release:

- **A new user turn that starts with a summary prefix is skipped.** LCM-X takes it for its own summary carrier and does not store it ([#1003](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1003)).
- **Rows appended after a shorter host view are not stored when they carry no host timestamps.** The fix needs the next-stage message classifier ([#1547](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1547), [#2058](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2058)).
- **The next-stage message classifier has six correctness defects.** They are to be fixed before it is wired into ingest; no path reaches them today ([#2288](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2288)).
- **A host startup stall past the 10 s deadline leaves LCM-X inactive.** No session in that host process is stored until the host restarts or the plugin is reloaded ([#2339](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2339)).
- **On an upgraded store with blank conversation IDs, a legacy row lets another conversation claim its receipt** ([#2423](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2423)).
- **In a session shared by two conversations, a new tool row is not stored** ([#2442](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2442)).
- **Rewrite-memory eviction after 16 notes can lose a merged prompt.** No supported path to 16 notes has been found ([#2476](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2476)).
- **Three routes can send rows to the wrong store if two profiles share one module copy.** Hermes loads one copy per home ([#2499](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2499)).
- **A host that edited a handed-over message in place could have the original skipped.** The ledger binds a digest taken before its transaction. No host writer is known to do this ([#2500](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2500)).
- **A cross-room /resume leaves the fold or snapshot owned by the old conversation** ([#2501](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2501)).
- **A partial summary deletion at /new leaves stored rows that no summary covers.** This is summary coverage, not a stored-row loss: the rows stay stored ([#2045](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2045)).

The remaining limits store extra copies, leave attribution incomplete, fail to honour an exclusion rule or slow a turn. They do not lose raw rows.

- **Some excluded parents still have stored children.** After an excluded parent rotates through compression, its delegated child is refused only on the shared route. Clone and prototype routes store the child despite `LCM_IGNORE_SESSION_PATTERNS` or the stateless exclusion patterns. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2070](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2070)).
- **Failed pre-compaction storage also duplicates a head.** After a failed input write before compaction, LCM-X stores the compacted head once more without a replay relation. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2440](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2440)).
- **Repeated recovery stores a user row again.** Two recovery fits of a repeated user turn followed by a restart store the projected user row once more, without a replay relation. Fix release not yet set ([#503](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/503)).
- **A later child restart stores kept rows again.** After rejecting a delegated child’s last-stored-row resume boundary, an identical rewritten view stores kept rows again without a replay relation. This takes one restart after a warm rejection or a second restart after a cold rejection; delegated-child restart resume is not reachable on the current host. The record of a child's last compaction outputs is also kept only in memory, so a restart of a delegated child stores its compacted head one extra time. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2439](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2439)).
- **Routing-key changes store the history again.** If the host assigns a live session a new routing key, such as a CLI handoff or resume from another room, the next warm turn stores the whole history again under the new conversation ID without replay relations. This was found in clone-run preflight and code reading and is not yet reproduced on main. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2461](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2461)).
- **Missing compression ancestry duplicates carried rows.** When a compression child’s ancestry cannot be verified and the host inserts a row before the resume point, the next ingest stores the parent’s final prompt and reply again without replay relations. This includes missing host state, missing parent or child records, a parent that did not end by compression or a fork marker; apparently complete ancestry also fails when an earlier process never wrote a needed predecessor record. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2463](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2463)).
- **A merged summary carrier creates an extra copy.** After the host merges LCM-X’s summary carrier into a user row, a warm replay from the start stores the merged carrier again, or stores copies from an otherwise unchanged view plus appended rows. Other middle-of-history edits do not belong to this limit. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1961](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1961)).
- **An unstamped restart replay stores old rows again.** The first ingest after restart can store another copy while advancing past a replayed prefix. This limit requires matching earlier rows in order, an earlier timestamped copy and a new copy with `observed_at` NULL; replay from position zero is handled by the new replay-link fix. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674)).
- **A rewritten unstamped view is stored again.** An ended engine’s final flush stores an unstamped view again after a resumed engine rewrites it, or a rewrite after a cold-start retry is stored again. A view with an additional host insertion or reordering is outside this limit. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2203](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2203)).
- **An unanswered prompt becomes part of a composite.** After a restart before the reply, the unanswered prompt and the next prompt are stored together as a composite row beside the next prompt’s own row. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#849](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/849)).
- **Rotation mapping can stall compaction.** A rotation leaves rows without the mapping compaction needs, so compaction stops making progress. A cold resend after a held fit-only rotation also stores predecessor rows again; those copies now carry `possible_replay_of` links across the recorded rotation chain, except the re-emitted summary marker. Planned fix for the remaining mapping and store-growth limits: v0.30.x ([#2029](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2029)).
- **Unstamped histories with existing copies grow on every restart.** On a host that sends no message timestamps, a session that already holds later exact copies of some rows stores its replayed history once more at each restart. Each extra copy has a possible-replay link. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#588](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/588)).
- **Earlier ledger-off copies cannot anchor borrowed-timestamp links.** Borrowed-timestamp linking cannot see a copy stored while `LCM_INGEST_LEDGER` was off. It can therefore link to a different bound copy when complete bindings would have left the attribution ambiguous; no row or per-key count changes. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2443](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2443)).
- **A late tool call stores its result twice.** When a tool call's row was not stored at its turn, a later ingest that brings the call (typically after a restart or a rebind, when the host sends its full history) stores the call once and its result a second time, without a replay relation. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2468](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2468)).
- **A persistent evidence fault can store the last row again.** After an evidence-read fault that persists past its retry (or a busy error followed by a one-off evidence-read fault, which gets no retry), the fail-open path can store the already-stored last row once more, shifted by a timestamped insert before it. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2374](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2374)).
- **Unstamped reply histories are stored again after an edit-and-resend and a restart.** On a host that sends replies without timestamps, a cold restart after an edit-and-resend stores the session's whole unstamped reply history again (41 copies after 40 turns in our test), without replay relations. Replies with host timestamps are not affected, and v0.29.1 and v0.29.2 behave the same. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2479](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2479)).
- **A restart right after a fit-only compaction can save the summary again.** After a compaction that only trimmed the conversation to fit, if the host keeps the trimmed list and the agent restarts before LCM-X next saves the session, one extra copy of LCM-X's summary joined to the first kept message can be saved as a plain message. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2118](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2118)).
- **A to-do list merged with your next message can be saved again.** The host can merge a saved to-do list with your next message into one combined message. When that combined message splits cleanly into earlier saved messages of the same session, LCM-X now links it to them with `composite_of`. After a conversation ends and resumes, though, the combined message is saved again with no link. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2488](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2488)).
- **A message can be saved twice after certain compaction passes.** After an overflow-recovery pass, or a compaction whose compacted messages were all hidden ones, if the host commits the rewritten conversation and restarts before the next compaction, a message can be saved again with no replay link. This has not been reproduced yet. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2134](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2134)).
- **A reused tool-call ID far apart can save a pair twice after a restart.** If a session reuses a tool-call ID for the same call and result more than 64 saved rows later, a restart can save that pair a second time without a replay link. No natural way to trigger this has been shown; our test forces it. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2197](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2197)).
- **A failed hand-off read can save a carried message again.** If LCM-X cannot read the previous session's record during a hand-off, a carried-over message can be saved again without a replay link. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2490](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2490)).
- **A kept message with a model-switch note can be saved again.** After a compaction, when the conversation is picked up again, a kept message that starts with a model-switch note and is shown with an extra leading space can be saved again, along with the next carried-over message. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2431](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2431)).
- **Older databases without conversation IDs can save a tool pair twice.** On older databases with no conversation IDs recorded, a tool call and its result can be saved twice after a restart. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2436](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2436)).
- **An insert into a just-compacted conversation can save the latest reply again.** If the app inserts a message without a timestamp into a conversation that a compaction has just moved to a new session, and the latest reply also has no timestamp, LCM-X can save that reply a second time. Without the app's session database, the carried-over earlier prompts can be saved again too. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2491](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2491), [#2463](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2463)).
- **A few compaction and setting-change paths save a marked extra copy.** After certain compactions, a restart can save LCM-X's summary or the compacted input again, marked as a copy: when the compaction's saved record is out of date, when a compaction that moved the conversation to a new session (a non-default setting) is followed by a restart before the new session starts, or when a restart comes before a new compaction is adopted. Changing the redaction setting before LCM-X first saves a session with the ingest ledger on can also save one marked extra copy, once. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1286](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286), [#758](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/758)).
- **A tool call with a long wrapped encoded block can be stored again at each restart.** A tool call whose arguments hold line-wrapped base64 of 4,096 characters or more, and its result, are stored once more at every cold restart in two cases: on a store written before v0.30.0; and, on any store, after the host changed that call's arguments in place. A call that v0.30.0 stored itself and that the host sends again unchanged is stored once. No row is lost; in the measurement in #2550, at most the first extra copy was linked as a possible replay, and the other copies were not marked. No supported Hermes version is known to change a stored call's arguments. Both cases also occur in v0.29.2. Planned fix: v0.30.1 ([#2550](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2550)).
- **Rolling back to v0.29.2 stores a saved tool result once more.** v0.30.0 stores the full content of a tool result that Hermes saved to a file. v0.29.2 knows such a result only as its short marker, so after a rollback it stores the tool call and the marker once more, the first time the host replays that history. Nothing is lost. The copy is not linked to the first one, and it does not grow on later replays or on upgrading again. Planned: link these copies on re-upgrade in v0.30.1 ([#2552](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2552)).
- **A saved tool result that was stored as its marker stays a marker.** v0.29.2 stored a large tool result that Hermes had saved to a file as the short marker Hermes leaves in the conversation. After the upgrade, v0.30.0 keeps that row as it is and does not add the saved file's content. The cases under the upgrade item below are the exception. The same holds for a result whose file was missing when v0.30.0 first stored it, for one whose payload file LCM-X could not write then, and, with sensitive-pattern redaction on, for a result saved under Hermes's home whose preview held text that redaction rewrites: the row stays a marker afterwards. The marker and its preview are what the model was shown; nothing the host sent is lost. Other results whose file is present when v0.30.0 stores them are stored in full ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)).
- **A reused call ID with an identical marker can be stored once more.** If a host reuses a tool call ID and repeats the identical saved-output marker, and the store holds that marker as a marker (see the item above), a replay that starts at a different point in the history stores one more copy of it. This happens once; a later replay adds nothing, and no host row is lost. No supported Hermes version is known to reuse a call ID this way ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)).
- **After an upgrade from v0.29.2, a saved tool result can be stored a second time.** On the first replay of a conversation after the upgrade, a tool call and its saved tool result can be stored once more, while the saved file still exists. At default settings two cases are known: the result was saved in Hermes's spillover folder and its preview holds an inline image or other data URI, or it was saved in the system temp folder with Windows line ends (Hermes saved results there only up to 0.20.4, and LCM-X supports Hermes 0.21.3 and later, so this second case affects no supported setup). Other settings can add cases of the same kind (a larger preview size set in Hermes, for example); that comes from reading the code and was not run. It happens once; later replays add nothing, and nothing is lost. Planned fix: v0.30.1 ([#2558](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2558)).
- **A helper agent's saved tool result can be stored one extra time.** LCM-X normally recognises a saved tool result by its marker. When a helper agent's history no longer lines up with its stored rows (the host trimmed or rewrote it, or after the helper agent's own compaction), LCM-X matches rows by counting them and compares the result's content instead. There, a result whose saved file is missing or was rewritten, or a reused tool call ID, is stored one extra time in total. No row is lost ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)).
- **A helper agent's row with an inline encoded block is stored more than once.** When a delegated helper agent's tool call holds an inline encoded block in its arguments, or a list-form row holds one in its content, LCM-X moves the block out when it stores the row, and at the next handover the stored row no longer matches what the host sends. The row is then stored again: one extra copy in a live helper session and at its end, up to two where rows are matched by counting, and up to three after the helper agent's own compaction. The copies stop after the second handover, and no row is lost. v0.29.2 does not store helper-agent sessions at all. Planned fix: v0.30.1 ([#2559](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2559)).
- **With redaction on, a saved tool result whose preview holds redacted text is kept as its marker, and its conversation can be stored again after a restart.** Sensitive-pattern redaction is off by default. With it on, a tool result saved under Hermes's home whose preview holds text that redaction rewrites is stored as its marker: LCM-X keeps the marker and its preview, not the saved file's full text. When the preview ends inside a secret, a first part of it that is too short for a pattern to match stays in the stored preview. On a replay after a restart whose assistant and tool rows carry no timestamps, rows of that conversation can then be stored again, at each such replay; v0.29.2 stores the same rows or more. A replay that carries timestamps on every row stores nothing twice, except when the rewritten text is a password, which redaction replaces without keeping a fingerprint, and the replay sends only part of the history; rows are then stored again, fewer than in v0.29.2. No row is lost. v0.29.2 also keeps only the marker and its preview, with the same short first part. A store that the release candidates rc1 to rc5 wrote with redaction on has two more effects, described under **Upgrade**. Planned fix: v0.30.1 ([#2604](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2604)).
- **While LCM-X cannot write its payload files, a replayed conversation that holds a saved tool result can be stored again.** If payload files cannot be written for a longer time (a full disk, or a payload folder that cannot be written to) while the database stays writable, a replay after a restart that sends only part of the history, and whose assistant and tool rows carry no timestamps, stores rows of such a conversation again at each replay, as v0.29.2 does. After the fault clears, a replay that sends only part of the history stores rows once more, and only once: with timestamps on every row, the tool call and its result, or the result alone when the replay starts at the result; without timestamps on assistant and tool rows, three rows, or two when the replay starts at the result. For a result under Hermes's home, v0.29.2 stores nothing again in the first case and stores rows again at every replay in the second. No row is lost ([#2605](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2605)).
- **A conversation stored with payload externalization turned off can be stored again on a replay.** Payload externalization is on by default. For a conversation that was stored with it off and holds a saved tool result, a replay after a restart stores rows of it again in 7 of the 12 replay forms tested: 5 with it still off, and 2 after it was turned on again. The copies can grow with each replay. No row is lost. v0.29.2 stores the same or more in every form. Planned fix: v0.30.2 ([#2597](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2597)).
- **One slow first turn after a restart on an affected session.** When one stored tool row carries only a name, the check at a cold start holds the store's write lock for about 4.3 s on a 2,000-row session in our measurement (an upper bound, taken on a shared machine). No data is affected. Planned fix: v0.30.1 ([#2258](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2258)).
- **The opt-in event recorder can keep one database file open until cleanup.** When the recorder replaces its database connection or hits a read error, it drops the old connection without closing it, so the file handle stays open until Python’s garbage collection runs. No data is affected. The recorder is off by default. Planned fix: v0.30.1 ([#2642](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2642)).
- **A crash after a compaction rotation, over ACP on upstream Hermes, can store one user turn twice.** The fault cells show it on both v0.29.2 and v0.30.0. Fix release not yet set ([#2507](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2507)).
- **After a crash during an upgrade from v0.27.0, a composite row is kept beside its replayed parts.** The fault cells show it on both v0.29.2 and v0.30.0 ([#1506](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1506)).
- **An equal-identity omission alignment can store a kept row twice.** This is the part of #1451 that stays open for v0.30.x ([#1451](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1451)).

Duplicate attribution requires the recorded ingest route and both store IDs; restart replay also requires the restart record. Timestamp absence alone does not establish a cause.

Six more limits affect only what the model sees in its prompt or what search and recall return; they do not lose or copy a stored row.

- **Turns can drop out of the prompt after rejected summaries.** If two summaries in a row are rejected and the maintenance sweep runs out of time, compaction pauses for 600 seconds. While it pauses, turns that no summary covers yet can drop out of the model's prompt, and the end of the pause does not bring them back. They stay stored, and recall can still reach them. Fix release not yet set ([#2272](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2272)).
- **After a host restart, turns since the first compaction drop out of the model's view.** Only in a conversation that has a compaction child (Hermes's legacy rotating compaction, `compression.in_place: false`, now or earlier; the default in-place mode creates none): on Hermes v0.21.6 to v0.23.1 over ACP (by our reading of the source; not run on a release; seen on two pinned upstream builds), any restart of the host, clean or after a crash, resumes the conversation as it was before its first compaction. Turns since then are no longer sent to the model, and default recall (scoped to the current session) does not reach their raw rows. Their rows remain in LCM-X's store, except the rows of a turn interrupted by a hard kill (#2624). This is a host defect, tracked upstream in NousResearch/hermes-agent#148047; v0.29.2 behaves the same. After the #2624 fix ships in v0.30.1, this stays open, and a conversation that is never loaded again keeps its named limit ([#2626](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2626)).
- **Two recall-size defects.** One is the hits-only budget for snippets, which lets a response pass its size cap; the other is a per-call limit of 1e999, which raises an error instead of falling back to the default. v0.29.2 has both. The fix is merged on main ([PR #2620](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2620)) and ships in v0.30.1.
- **`lcm_grep` searches only the first 512 KB of a saved tool output.** The rest of the file is kept but is not searched. Fix release not yet set ([#2518](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2518)).
- **A value that appears only in a tool call's input is not searchable.** The call is stored, but search does not find a value that appears only in its arguments. Fix release not yet set ([#2519](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2519)).
- **In a saved tool output, `lcm_grep` finds a query only where it appears word for word.** A quoted phrase, the same words in another order or one extra word finds nothing in a saved tool output, although message search matches such queries term by term. In the read-only MCP reader, hybrid and semantic modes do not search saved tool outputs in the default scope (an explicit `content_scope` is served by full-text search); use `mode='full_text'` there. The first part is fixed on main ([#2586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2586), [PR #2587](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2587)); the second is tracked in [#2592](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2592), with no fix release set yet.

## Qualification

v0.30.0 is qualified on its final release candidate, v0.30.0-rc6, which has the same code. As a minor release, it runs a smoke stage first and then the full gauntlet. No result from an earlier candidate carries over: the final candidate's fixes changed what LCM-X stores for a saved tool result, so every row runs again on it. GA needs every gate below, except where a v0.30.0-only row of the release spec or a named release-manager ruling says otherwise; each such row is named below with its outcome. No result below comes from a customer session. In the scorecard, a cell with no gate result in this release is empty.

- Nothing lost, the certifying driven run: **PASS after hand checks**. All 8 bars pass: 0 lost rows, 0 silent extra copies, 0 exempted extra copies and 0 sessions stored with no rows; delegated helper agents: 12 of 12. Of 1,166 rows expected, 1,174 are stored, with 0 missing and 11 visible extra copies (7 composite rows, 4 replay copies); 3 stored rows each hold two expected rows, which closes the count. The run covered 454 turns, 31 compactions, 12 restarts and 127 tool calls. Three blind readers cleared all 11 hand checks; those questions were set after the run, so this is an independent reading of the evidence, not a pre-registered test. It is one driven run on one host build: it does not show other hosts, the reference agent, crash windows outside the driver’s operations, or #2624 and #2626 ([receipt](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1931)).
- Required CI checks on the final candidate, read back and not re-run: **PASS**. All nine are green: eight on the candidate’s head, and the `differential` check on the head of [PR #2618](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2618) (the release-prep pull request). Of 54 check runs, 52 succeeded; the 2 failures are the first reliability-matrix run below. The required checks run the whole test suite apart from its latency tests, in four shards on each Python version in the CI matrix, against a stub of the host’s interface; the suite on real host builds is Phase B, below.
- Smoke stage on the final candidate: **PASS**, on reference hosts, CI and synthetic rows. It found no P0 or P1 defect; #2624 and #2626, found during it, are under **Known issues**.
  - reliability matrix on all seven hosts, gating on new failures: **PASS on the second run**. The first run reported 2 new failing cells (both errors), classed as instrument and environment faults; that result stays visible. Each of the two cells passed on the other six hosts and in the base run. The second run: 0 new and 0 untracked failures;
  - the 12 hands-on fault-cell pairs, v0.29.2 against the candidate, with no unmatched failure: **no regression**, raw FAILs kept: 6 PASS, 3 KNOWN (raw FAIL visible) and 3 UNSUPPORTED. KNOWN: the in-process upgrade-crash cell on upstream Hermes fails 3 of 3 on both versions, 9 of 9 pairings equal ([#1506](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1506)); the ACP crash cell on upstream Hermes fails 3 of 3 on both, 9 of 9 equal ([#2507](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2507); its “nothing missing” holds only when the host had not saved the interrupted reply, see #2624); one ACP crash cell on Hermes 0.21.5 failed 1 of 3 runs on the candidate and 0 of 3 on v0.29.2, and over recorded runs 5 of 10 on candidates and 4 of 10 on v0.29.2, with host-parity checks agreeing in 40 of 40 (#861, the scorer defect above). The default in-place compaction mode is shown unaffected, for storage and for a conversation that was never rotated, by a run on seven host builds of the harness pull request's tree on main, not on the candidate (the in-place cell of [#2627](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2627));
