  - the rollback replay of a saved tool result (the named rollback limit, [#2552](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2552)), with exactly its 2 expected extra rows, 0 lost rows and no growth: **matches the named limit**. Two cells stored 11 rows for 9 handed (2 extra, 0 lost, no growth); three cells stored 9;
  - the write-fault probe: with the payload folder unwritable, no row lost that v0.29.2 stores, no copy added by a delegated child, and no replay surplus over v0.29.2 that keeps growing ([#2599](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2599)): **PASS**, none of its four stop conditions hit. In both fault cells of each kind, the candidate stored all 13 handed rows, including the final reply (v0.30.0-rc5: 12); live delegated-child copies: 1, 1, 1, 1, 1; one bounded replay cell gained two extra rows from the third replay on and never more over six replays (#2172); with payload externalization off, 12 of 13 on both versions (#2547); from the second replay on, the candidate stores 4 rows fewer than v0.29.2 (#2605). These are engine-level probes on a stub host with synthetic rows;
  - the redaction probe: with sensitive-pattern redaction on, no row lost that v0.29.2 stores and no count above v0.29.2’s ([#2603](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2603)): **PASS by a release-manager ruling**; one of its stop conditions is hit only as worded. Every spillover cell stores exactly 11 handed rows on both versions;
  - D1 recall with embeddings off, fast tier, 500 questions: 0 unexplained per-question changes: **PASS**. 0 recall changes and 0 full-text changes over 500 of 500 questions against v0.29.2, and 0 discordant rows in a same-build repeat;
  - Phase B, the independent review sweep of the full diff (501 files): **clear**. 88 of 88 independent reads, no confirmed defect and no new claim above P3 (one carried P2, #2500, is listed under **Known issues**). Four unmeasured cost leads are recorded on [#2504](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2504);
  - the delegated-child saved-result case ([#2539](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2539)): **not reproduced** at default settings (7 cells, 3 runs each, one stored row per handed row; a second route: 30 passed, 8 expected failures under #2547 and #2543). Recorded only, with no verdict: #2558, 9 rows for 7 handed, no growth, 0 lost; #2559, live child: 2 copies after the first handover and no more after the second, with the off-current cells dropping the final row on both versions (#2543); #2550, 11 rows for 7 handed, +2 per cold replay;
  - mini rows, which give no receipt and no credit to their full rows: 30 D4 questions **PASS** with 0 net losses; one D7 seed **PASS** (not gating); 25 D1 questions with local embeddings, which runs alongside the full rows and is not part of the smoke-stage verdict: **PASS**, with no changed result against v0.29.2 and no recall that timed out or reported itself unhealthy.
- Full rows. For v0.30.0 alone, the release spec lets two of them leave the gate under five recorded conditions: D1 with local embeddings (500 questions) when the first, second, third and fifth hold, and D4/D8 when all five hold. The conditions: two independent code reviews find nothing against v0.29.2 that can change what these rows store or return, apart from one full-text retry that can only add results; the fast-tier D1 row above shows 0 changed answers; the two short recall rows pass on the candidate; none of their recall responses used that retry; and these notes list every default-on change in recall and search. The two short rows do not record whether a response used the retry, so the fourth condition could not be shown on the candidate, and D4/D8 stayed in the gate as a paired sample of 100 questions, as the spec provides. The other four conditions hold for the candidate; for the third, both short rows passed (see the mini rows above). A row that leaves the gate is reported here as not run; it runs after GA on the GA tree, and its result is published. D1 with local embeddings (500 questions): **not run** (raw verdict UNRUN, which is not green). It left the gate under the conditions above, and no pass is claimed.
- D4/D8, the paired sample of 100 recall questions: **PASS**, all pre-declared bars clear. The candidate answered 87 of 100, v0.29.2 86 and a candidate repeat 86. Against v0.29.2, 3 answers differ (2 gained, 1 lost; p = 1.0); against its repeat, 1 differs. The preference part passes (30 questions: 25 against 25, repeat 24). 0 of 122 question ids degraded in all three arms. Reader: gpt-6.1-sol. The pre-declared bars (sha256 `5fe45c6a07f11f03dd4101954179e76c2bc1bf54dea46a916ceebc0057201150`): FAIL on a failed run check, on D4's blocking test against v0.29.2 (exact two-sided McNemar p < 0.05 with more losses than gains), or on losses minus gains above 3 in the 6 abstention or the 18 knowledge-update questions; INCONCLUSIVE if the candidate and its repeat differ on more than 5 of the 100 questions; the 30 preference questions are their own row, which fails when wins minus losses falls below -min(2, max(1, d)), d being the candidate's disagreements with its repeat on them. The sample is not a D4 or D8 verdict: the full D4 and D8 rows did not run before GA and run after it as monitoring rows. No D4 or D8 pass is claimed.
- D2, D3 and their prospective A/A: **not run** (raw verdict UNRUN, which is not green), by the release spec’s v0.30.0-only D2/D3 row ([PR #2631](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2631); trackers [#2272](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2272), [#2273](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2273), the replay harness's handling of wall-clock holds, [#2274](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2274), the service classification that decides whether a replay is service-invalid). The row applies only if D7 passes with bars 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 judged, and both D5-B cells pass their lossless bars; otherwise the unrun D2 blocks GA: **both hold, so the row applies**. No facts-kept bar against v0.29.2 is judged in v0.30.0, although the release changes compaction and summariser code (`compaction.py`, `summary_attempt.py`; for example #1335, #960, #2101, #2128). D7’s bar 4, facts kept, recorded and not judged: mean 0.900 at checkpoint 304 (seeds 0.883, 0.900, 0.917). The v0.29.2 tree’s facts-kept mean and per-seed values from the same runner, reader and seeds, recorded and not judged: 0.917 (0.917, 0.900, 0.933). The candidate is 0.017 lower; the line fixed before that comparison ran makes a gap above 0.10 a release finding, so this is none.
- Two test-kit rows were removed from the selection on 2026-11-11, before GA (#2496): the occurrence grader, which has never run in any release (it needs 150 GB free and a remote worker), and a carry-over row that can only answer “rerun”. Raw verdicts: UNRUN; neither grants a pass. The engine-level regression test that #1969 added (`tests/invariants/test_issue_1967_restart_pair_timestamps.py`) runs with the suite at every release candidate.
- Phase B, the probe matrix: **raw FAIL, not green**. It is dispositioned under the Phase B differential rule; no respin. Its scorer reads 10 PASS, 28 PRE-EXISTING and 4 REGRESSION of 42 cells. The differential reading finds 12 equal, 4 subset and 0 worse. In the 4 cells the candidate stores v0.29.2’s rows minus one extra copy: no row lost or added, order kept. The cause is the ingest ledger’s cold-start cursor ([PR #2151](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2151), part of #2055), shown by a control with the ledger off; the operator line is under **Upgrade**. It shows stored-row identity in 42 synthetic cells on one host build (0.21.3); it does not show the skip guards for every neighbouring shape, and neither version is free of duplicates in these cells.
- Phase B, the host-suite comparison on seven real host builds: **not green**, shipped under a v0.30.0-only row of the release spec ([PR #2648](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2648)); no respin. Each host build runs the whole test suite in one process under its own Python, and the candidate’s failing tests are compared with v0.29.2’s on the same build. On the five Hermes 0.21.x builds, the union of every job that ran to the end (a rule fixed before the last run) has 26 new failing tests on each build and one more on the Python 3.12 build. On the two Python 3.14 upstream builds, the candidate’s first runs ran out of file descriptors under CI’s limit of 1024, which v0.29.2’s did not; a measurement traced the extra use to test connections left for garbage collection ([#2643](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2643)) and one handle the opt-in recorder, off by default, can leave open, a P3 product defect ([#2642](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2642)). Both versions were re-run there at 4096: 27 new failing tests on each, all of them among the five builds’ new failures. Every new failure is a defect of a test or of the test kit, tracked for v0.30.1: a new test helper removes the host variables from the test process (19 failures, [#2636](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2636)), a probe waits for a log line that ingest no longer writes (7, [#2637](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2637): on every build all 7 fail at that wait, and the stored rows equal v0.29.2’s on the one build compared, in a local run), and a new test cannot make an import fail on an editable host install ([#2638](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2638)). With the environment intact, the 19 tests of #2636 pass on the candidate in local runs on five of the seven builds (not confirmed on the CI runner). On the Python 3.14 builds, 19 tests that pass on v0.29.2 skip on the candidate: 15 because of the same helper (they pass with the environment intact) and 4 that now assert the fix for [#2116](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2116) as an expected failure (see **Known issues**). On the five 0.21.x builds, 18 tests skip the same way, the same 18 on every build, all among those 19. No failing test is untracked.
- D5-B, the two clone cells: **not green on two bars**, shipped under a v0.30.0-only row of the release spec ([#2635](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2635)). The judged lossless bar passes in both cells, with 0 lost and 0 duplicated rows. Not green: tracebacks with an LCM-X frame, 7 and 8 against a bar of 0, every one the host-caught refusal to detach the engine from a background-review fork ([#1675](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1675); v0.29.2: 7 and 9); and the doctor, with 2 and 3 warnings and no failed check. Every other bar passes.
- Phase C, the soak on seven host builds: **not green on two bars**, under the same kind of row ([#2635](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2635)). Lossless passes on all seven, with 0 missing and 0 duplicated rows; each cell committed 10 to 17 compactions; recall probes are 3 of 3 exact on every host; the engine logs hold no error line. Not green: the doctor (warnings on every host, no failed check) and caught host traces (6 to 9 detach refusals per cell; v0.29.2: 7 to 12). One cell is a re-run: its first attempt had no result, because the host chose a provider address the test kit does not configure and no compaction came due. Provider failures the engine handled: 11 rejected summary results over the seven cells and, in the re-run cell, 3 summary calls that timed out; each compaction then committed or stopped.
- D5, the clone run: **not run** for this release, by the release spec's "v0.30.0 only" D5 row ([PR #2646](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2646)). Since v0.29.2, D5's integrity gate has been a scripted clone run: the release candidate and v0.29.2 replay the same workload and restarts from one snapshot of the reference agent's store. The runner is built and the snapshot was taken on 2026-11-12. Its preflights ran with v0.29.2 in both arms and found three defects in the instrument (counts in [D5-PREFLIGHT-RECEIPT.md](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.30.0/D5-PREFLIGHT-RECEIPT.md)): an externalized output that differs between two arms of the same tree, a host pin without the git metadata the replay needs, and a pinned host that makes neither host rewrite the workload requires. The first and the last need instrument changes that apply from the next release candidate, so the clone run moves to v0.30.1 ([#2647](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2647)). No canary window ran: the reference agent was not moved to this release candidate, and it moves to v0.30.0 after the release as post-release monitoring. A real-store check ran instead: this release and v0.29.2 each ran the clone run's workload on the same snapshot, without binds or replays. In both, all 554,740 snapshot rows stayed present and unchanged, in order and in their sessions; no log line broke a publication invariant; and the doctor, integrity and quick checks reported no failure. One check failed in both alike: the host database's schema check finds version 32 where the pinned host build expects 31, a version the snapshot already had before either ran (an instrument defect, recorded on #2647). The candidate showed no LCM-X traceback or doctor warning that v0.29.2 lacks, and made one summary call fewer (50 provider calls against 51). Rows written during the workload are not measured by this check ([REAL-STORE-CHECK.md](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.30.0/REAL-STORE-CHECK.md)). It is not D5 and is not a D5 pass. D5's latency is still gated by Phase C, D5-B and D7.
- D6, recorded only: from C4, the `OFF` recall row (0 flips in 500 questions against v0.29.2). The other D6 rows (`VOYAGE-TRACKER` recall and QA, the `OFF` QA row, the continuity suite and the external arms) did not run on this candidate and run after the release as monitoring rows ([#2649](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2649)). Host cells: **PASS** in all four cells, with every bar met and no misses. The cells ran once; the scoring step ran a second time after a setup error in our own post step.
- Same-store recall latency ([#1586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1586)): **NO_REGRESSION** on the second run, the run that counts. Candidate to v0.29.2 ratios 0.998 to 1.001; the highest upper bound is 1.008. All 820 recalls ran with full coverage. The first run is published as UNPROVEN: its warm-up did not wait for the embedding model, so the first recalls of each block ran without semantic search, in both versions. Its bar: every one-sided 95% upper bound of the candidate-to-base ratio, at p50 and p90, is at most 1.15, for both query classes, with no censored percentile, no more timeouts or degraded recalls on the candidate, no errors and the same coverage. It measures recall on the store used by the v0.29.1 row, in the state that row left it, on one thread with no compaction load; it does not measure the upgrade cost.

A later ruling ships v0.30.0 with it, listed under **Known issues**; the bar gates v0.30.1.

- D7, the compaction row (how often compaction runs, how long turns wait, rows kept through compaction, and facts kept against the previous release): **PASS**, in floor-pending mode. Bars 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 are judged and all met: 16.1 compactions per 100 turns (bar: at most 25); mean wait per turn 5.02 s (at most 15 s); 16.1% of turns waited (at most 25%); 0 dropped rows; compaction wall time p90 37.8 s (at most 120 s). Three seeds, 186 turns after the first compaction, 0 timeouts. The same row on the v0.29.2 tree, recorded and not judged: mean wait 5.24 s, wall time p90 38.2 s. Bar 4, facts kept, is recorded and not judged, because its floor needs a reader bridge that moves to v0.30.x ([#2492](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2492)). The release spec records this as a v0.30.0-only row, adopted before the candidate’s tag ([#2496](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2496), the tracker for these v0.30.0-only rows).
- D8, the delivery guards (abstention, facts that update, and LoCoMo's adversarial questions, each against the previous release): its gate form is the paired sample above, and the full row runs after GA; no D8 pass is claimed. Its noise check is the same build run twice. When the full row runs, D8 is read per dataset: where the check fails, D8 is not green there, and its published result says so and claims no D8 pass there. The check failed on every run in v0.29.0 and in both of v0.29.2's LongMemEval-S rounds, and its categories are small: one answer in the 30-question abstention set moves the score 3.3 points. Its replacement ([#2097](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2097)) is v0.30.x work. The release spec records this as a v0.30.0-only row, adopted before the candidate’s tag.
